A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and retain matching core methods and experiments. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original ImageNet experiments on membership inference, dataset inference, training-image extraction and privacy defenses, including appendix ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds VAR-CLIP evaluation, unified loss-attack experiments, additional diffusion-model evaluations and correlation analyses.

M1.justification: The conditional-output MIA features, MAR adjustments, normalized feature-sum DI, prefix-based extraction and output-noising defense are retained. v2 clarifies probability-based scoring and per-sample aggregation. The added unified Loss Attack serves as an evaluation control.

E1.justification: v1 excludes text-conditioned models from its privacy evaluation. v2 adds MIA and DI evaluation of VAR-CLIP trained on captioned ImageNet-1k (Appendix B.1, Table 6), extending conditioning requirements within the retained image domain.

E2.justification: v2 adds evaluated LFM and DiT-MoE models as supplementary diffusion reference architectures (Table 9), although explicitly excluding them from the primary comparison. The original LLM-MIA and DM-MIA comparator sets, including CLiD, remain.

E3.justification: Appendix C adds a common training-loss evaluation across 19 models, using random diffusion timesteps, fewer noise draws, training-style MAR masking and loss-only DI without DM-specific scoring. Table 7 additionally reports MIA accuracy. These are new controls; the main experiments retain 10,000 members and 10,000 nonmembers.

E4.justification: v2 adds cross-model correlation analysis of architecture, size and training duration, plus a unified-loss control testing whether leakage differences persist without tailored attacks (Appendices A and C). The original MAR ablations, DI aggregation ablation, mitigation experiments and prefix/SSCD analyses remain.

E5.justification: Appendix A.2 adds pairwise Pearson correlation estimation across 11 IARs and eight DMs. Both versions retain reporting over 100 randomized MIA experiments, uncertainty entries and Welch tests at 0.01. Changed numerical uncertainties do not establish increased repetitions.

E6.justification: The improved MAR results are substantially replaced: MAR-H Min-K% TPR changes from 49.19% to 3.40%, and AUC from 96.40 to 59.98 (v1 Tables 11–12; v2 Tables 16–17). SiT-XL/2 CLiD changes from 0.91% to 6.38% TPR and from 43.58 to 78.65 AUC, making SiT the strongest reported DM result. v2 also adds correlation, VAR-CLIP, unified-attack and additional DM results. The headline IAR attack and extraction outcomes remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The objectives, numbered MIA equations, DI null hypothesis and IID assumption are retained. The explicit conditional-probability difference clarifies the existing attack. New architectural explanations and empirical correlations introduce no substantive formal derivation, theorem or proof.

C1.justification: v2 narrows the broad IAR–DM privacy comparison to empirical findings under current attacks and models with similar FID. It also describes IAR image quality as matching or surpassing DMs. The three attack contributions and headline IAR outcomes remain.

C2.justification: New Appendix A offers mechanisms involving likelihood access, prediction targets and token-level signals. Expanded limitations discuss unavailable large-scale training data and confounding by model size, training duration, objectives and tokenizers. v2 also attributes VAR-CLIP leakage to richer conditioning and explicitly qualifies the proposed diffusion-based mitigation direction.

D1.justification: v2 newly tabulates DM parameter counts, training steps and batch sizes; supplies Min-K%, Min-K%++ and SURP search grids and selection rules; and documents the unified control and DI's MinMaxScaler implementation. This substantially expands reproducibility information. The code link, hardware disclosure and original IAR training details remain.

R1.justification: v2 adds diffusion-architecture background and citations, alongside references on privacy auditing and distribution mismatch. It explicitly distinguishes its attack from CLiD's loss-based scoring and fitted scaler, and removes the VAR-CLIP issue citation. The central research positioning is retained.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized rewrites to the abstract, introduction, attack explanations and conclusions, expands terminology explanations and reorganizes the opening appendices. The main section sequence and most existing exposition remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds a DI workflow diagram (Figure 4) and new correlation, comparison and model-detail tables (Tables 5–9). It restyles trade-off plots with square DM markers and separate legends, expands captions and consolidates appendix result tables into a denser layout. The extraction image galleries are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 resolves a serious internal inconsistency: its revised MAR-H Min-K% result of 3.40% agrees with the main tables, replacing v1's conflicting 49.19%. The unified-attack control, text-conditioned evaluation and fuller settings documentation substantially strengthen the evidence and reproducibility. Architectural causes remain unisolated, as Appendix B.2 acknowledges, so some mechanism interpretations remain inconclusive; nevertheless, the gains in consistency and empirical support are substantial.
